title: How can I implement a psych test that enables the player to customize gender, pronoun, personality type and love interest gender

posts.author: elang_S
posts.body:
After being sent an rpg maker mv steam key and officially confirmed that the key works. I am now upgraded to rpg maker mv
I'm using mv as opposed to vx ace because I needed the updated resolution (above 640x480p) that vx doesn't have natively
My first rpg maker mv question is, I want to implement a psych exam that serves as the player's main customizing setting
By meaning from this psych test it can enable the players to customize their gender, pronouns, what personality type they are and whether or not the love interests they pursue is male or female (depending on answer can make all love interests one gender or can manually pick their gender as the story progress)
Besides that the psych test (players can answer with a yes or no, a typing based answer, or pick and choose via point and click segment) will also determine what route they'll follow (there will be at least 9 love interests that's divided by 3 group prologues that depending on player choice will also determine from the 9 love interests who the player will focus on)
Because there's so many moving parts in this type of mechanic, what's the most apt way to implement this system?
Can plugins handle this or do you actually have to code this from scratch?

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
The precise details depend on how your test is scored, but basically you'd use switches and/or variables to store the responses, then present/apply the result based on those switches/variables.
A switch can be one of two values: on (true) or off (false). So it's ideal for storing yes/no, this-or-that values.
A variable typically stores an integer, so it can be used to store more complicated choices. E.g. "pick a colour: red, green, or blue" might store the answer as 1 (red), 2 (green), or 3 (blue). That variable can be referenced later on wherever necessary.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
First, a technicalish answer.
You could readily do this through Events and you don't need any plugins (depending on how you actually want the interaction to work). But it's possible that a plugin(s) could make it easier. I don't know because I don't use a lot of plugins.
As mentioned above, Switches and Variables are easy to use for yes/no answers or choice selection.
However, your typing-based answers would be more problematic since you would have to account for anything that the player types and somehow interpret that for your scoring of personality or whatever.
As far as the most apt way to implement this system, that would entirely depend on how you want to design it. First I would come up with all the things that are being determined by the process, what you are going to ask or present the player with to make those determinations, and how you want that experience to be. Those decisions seem instrumental in how the actual system would be designed and implemented.
Just for experience and fun, I did something a bit similar in my first and only Game Jam game where the player can answer scenario-based questions which ultimately determines if the player is Naughty or Nice. It was quite simple and I tried to make the Naughty and Nice options pretty obvious. But I'm sure even those questions could be debatable.
Now, a personal opinion so you can disregard the rest if you don't care about my opinion.
I would suggest...caution...if you are trying to use questions to designate someone's personality type and especially things like gender, pronouns, and love interests. As someone who has taken many personality tests in the professional world, they can be rather controversial, subjective, and some yield outright dubious results. And those were all designed by professionals who are supposed to know what they are doing.
Things like gender preference, pronouns, and romantic interests seem like things that would be better left to direct player choice/input. Because even choices that you think might obviously point in a specific direction can be subject to personal interpretation of the wording of the question.
With that being said, I can think of some types of questions that could be used to determine potential romantic interest paths, if done carefully, but (as a player), I would probably balk at having that used to extrapolate a "personality type".
Anyway, you can disregard that digression of personal opinion.
But again, I think it would be difficult for anyone to give you a good, specific answer on exactly how to approach this without knowing a lot more information, as I highlighted above.
Good luck on your project!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Oh, I missed the part about typing answers! That can be done via actor names: the
Name Input Processing
command lets the player input a new name for an actor with a gamepad-/touch-compatible interface.
Change Name
can be used to reset the current name before prompting for input. It's a bit limited but works well enough for short & simple answers.
Alternatively you could look for a suitable plugin, e.g.
MV/RS_TextArea.js at master · biud436/MV
This plugin package includes helpful features to get you on your way to create your game in RPG Maker MV. - biud436/MV
github.com
(If necessary,
regular expressions
can be used for matching complex patterns in text.)
